program.title: Beginner Cycling Fitness Foundation – Week 1
program.goal: Build aerobic base and knee-stable outdoor cycling capacity with off-bike trunk support

athlete_analysis.profile_summary: Beginner fitness cyclist, 1 session/week, 45-min outdoor bike sessions. Mild occasional knee discomfort on hills; 7h sleep, moderate stress. Ready for easy-duration progression with knee-friendly strength support.
primary_constraints: Mild knee discomfort on hills—avoid steep climbing, high cadence sprints, or fatigue-induced poor pedal mechanics
Beginner handling skills—prioritize safe, flat/rolling routes; route familiarity over intensity
Single training day—compress off-bike work into 45-min session or use short daily mobility snacks
sport_demands: Aerobic endurance: easy 20–30 min rides, building toward 45–60 min over weeks
Trunk and upper-back endurance: posture stability under seated load
Hip and glute stability: pedal mechanics, knee tracking, hip-hinge support on hills
athlete_analysis.block_priority: Establish safe cycling confidence, basic bike control, and consistent easy-ride tolerance. Off-bike sessions build glute, hip, and trunk capacity to reduce knee load. Knee symptom tracking is primary feedback loop.

weeks.theme: Establish easy-ride routine with knee-stable strength prep

workouts.title: Easy outdoor fitness ride + strength prep
sport_transfer: Seated aerobic capacity and pedal rhythm at conversational intensity
Safe braking, shifting, and turning on flat-to-rolling terrain
Glute and hip engagement to maintain knee alignment and reduce hill-strain
workouts.why_this_session: Build aerobic habit, confirm route safety and knee symptom response, and establish baseline endurance tolerance before adding duration.

warmup.name: Dead Bug
warmup.purpose: Activate core and low-back stability before seated cycling load

warmup.name: Band Lateral Walk
warmup.purpose: Activate lateral hip and glute to support knee alignment during pedal stroke

warmup.name: Glute Bridge
warmup.purpose: Establish glute firing and hip extension before riding

main_work.name: Outdoor easy-paced cycling
main_work.purpose: Build aerobic base and cycling confidence on safe, familiar flat-to-rolling route
main_work.load_guidance: Easy effort; able to speak in full sentences; pedal at natural cadence (90–100 rpm)

main_work.name: Goblet Squat
main_work.purpose: Build leg strength and squat mechanics to support hill climbing and knee stability
main_work.load_guidance: Light to moderate dumbbell or kettlebell; feet shoulder-width; chest upright

main_work.name: Cable Pull-Through
main_work.purpose: Strengthen hip hinge and posterior chain to support pedal power and knee comfort on hills
main_work.load_guidance: Moderate cable load; face away from low pulley; hinge from hips

main_work.name: Farmer's Carry
main_work.purpose: Build trunk stiffness and posture endurance to support seated cycling posture
main_work.load_guidance: Light dumbbells or kettlebells; stand tall; walk in straight line

cooldown.name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
cooldown.purpose: Release hip flexor tightness from cycling and sitting

cooldown.name: Bird Dog
cooldown.purpose: Reinforce anti-rotation stability and core endurance

injury_modifications: If knee discomfort increases during ride, stop and return home; log duration and hill incline in symptom diary
Avoid steep climbs or sustained high cadence (>110 rpm) until knee baseline is established
If pain worsens 24 hours post-ride, skip strength session and do light mobility only; consult medical clearance

weeks.progression_rule: Complete 1 full easy-paced outdoor ride (20–30 min) on Monday. Off-bike work focuses on glute activation, trunk bracing, and hip mobility to support pedal mechanics and knee comfort. No intensity; all RPE easy.

program.nutrition_focus: Adequate total calories and carbohydrate to support 20–30 min easy ride recovery and off-bike strength work. Hydration during ride if temperature >20°C.
recovery_focus: Sleep consistency: maintain 7-hour baseline to support aerobic adaptation
Post-ride: light stretching, hydration, carb + protein within 30–60 min
Daily posture breaks: 2–3 min hip and thoracic mobility snacks to offset saddle and desk time
safety_notes: Pre-ride bike check: brakes, tires, shifting, helmet fit before every session
Route: flat or gentle rolling terrain, familiar roads, low traffic; avoid hills or technical sections until week 3+
Knee tracking: pedal in smooth circles; if knee pain spikes mid-ride, reduce cadence or stop
24-hour symptom diary: log ride duration, route terrain, knee pain (0–10), and next-day response
assumptions: Bike is roadworthy and fits rider; mild saddle soreness is expected first 1–2 weeks
Outdoor environment is safe and accessible for solo 20–30 min rides
Strength equipment (dumbbells, kettlebells, cable machine) is available or substitutable with bodyweight/band alternatives
No medical contraindication to easy cycling; knee pain is mechanical and responds to load management

workout_titles: Easy outdoor fitness ride + strength prep
